c.tagline: Africa's diplomatic capital atop the Rift Valley highlands.

taxi.fareNote: Most street taxis (shared or contract) negotiate a fare before departure since many lack working meters; ride-hailing apps (RIDE, Feres) show a fixed app-calculated price upfront.

emergency.note: Response times can be slow; ask your hotel to help coordinate, and for serious issues use a private clinic (e.g., Bethzatha, CURE, or Landmark General Hospital) or contact your embassy.

hood_landmark.Bole: Edna Mall, Bole Road, Addis Ababa
hood_landmark.Piassa: Saint George Cathedral, Piassa, Addis Ababa
hood_landmark.Old Airport: Bisrate Gabriel Church, Old Airport, Addis Ababa

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing around the Merkato market and on minibuses; caution at night

hood_desc: The city's modern hub of high-rises, malls, restaurants, and nightlife, minutes from the airport; best for business travelers and first-time visitors wanting convenience.
Addis Ababa's diplomatic and UN quarter, home to the African Union and UNECA compounds and many business hotels; suits conference-goers, NGO staff, and diplomats.
The historic old town with Italian-era arcaded buildings, Merkato-adjacent markets, and budget guesthouses; ideal for backpackers, history buffs, and photographers.
Central business core anchored by Meskel Square, with luxury hotels, the National Museum, and easy light-rail access; good for travelers wanting a central, walkable-ish base.
A quieter, leafy residential and embassy area popular with expats and longer-stay visitors, with boutique hotels and good restaurants away from downtown bustle.
lodging: Doubletree By Hilton Addis Ababa Airport
Sheraton Addis, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Addis Ababa

water.note: Tap water is unreliable and often contaminated; drink bottled or boiled water only.

transit.pay: For the light rail, buy a paper ticket at the station window before entering the platform (distance-based fares of about 2-6 ETB). City buses are paid in cash to the conductor onboard. Ride-hailing apps like RIDE and Feres charge a fixed in-app fare.
transit.hours: Light rail and most city buses run roughly 06:00-22:00 daily; there is no late-night public transit, so use taxis or ride-hailing apps after dark.
transit.note: Rush-hour traffic is heavy; the light rail's two lines (Green: east-west, Blue: north-south) are often faster than buses or taxis for cross-town trips.

transit.m: Anbessa public bus into downtown (board just outside the terminal, ~25-40 min)

tip.r: A 10% tip is appreciated at restaurants when no service charge is included; rounding up is common for taxis; not expected for small everyday purchases.

food.name: Doro wat with injera
food.desc: Ethiopia's celebration stew: chicken and a hard-boiled egg simmered for hours in berbere and spiced butter, served on sour injera flatbread.

places.name: Yod Abyssinia Cultural Restaurant
places.note: Best-known cultural restaurant; strong doro wat with nightly music and dance.

places.name: 2000 Habesha Cultural Restaurant
places.note: Tukul-style hall, big traditional platters and live performances every evening.

places.name: Dashen Traditional Restaurant
places.note: Stone-walled traditional room that stays true to local flavours; loyal lunch crowd.

food.name: Kitfo
food.desc: Minced raw or lightly warmed beef whipped with mitmita chilli and niter kibbeh spiced butter, served with ayib cheese, gomen greens and kocho.

places.name: Yohannes Kitfo
places.note: Addis institution specialising in kitfo; go for leb leb (lightly cooked) if raw is too much.

places.name: Kategna Restaurant
places.note: Clean, modern room doing refined versions of the classics, kitfo included.

places.name: Dashen Traditional Restaurant
places.note: Traditional preparation with ayib and kocho, favoured by locals over tourists.

food.name: Tibs
food.desc: Cubes of beef, lamb or goat flash-fried with onion, rosemary, jalapeno and butter, often arriving still sizzling on a clay brazier.

places.name: Kategna Restaurant
places.note: Reliably good derek and awaze tibs; easy first stop for Ethiopian food.

places.name: Yod Abyssinia
places.note: Large menu of tibs styles served on shared injera platters.

places.name: Addis Ababa Restaurant
places.note: Traditional hut setting long recommended if you only have one dinner in town.

food.name: Shiro wat
food.desc: Silky ground-chickpea stew with berbere and garlic, bubbling in a clay dish. The everyday Ethiopian comfort food and the go-to fasting dish.

places.name: Kategna Restaurant
places.note: Its shiro is widely cited as among the best in Addis; also good tegabino.

places.name: Dashen Traditional Restaurant
places.note: Home-style shiro with fresh injera at local rather than tourist prices.

places.name: Yod Abyssinia
places.note: Good place to try shiro as part of a mixed vegetarian beyaynetu platter.

food.name: Beyaynetu (fasting platter)
food.desc: A wheel of vegan stews on injera: shiro, misir wat lentils, gomen, cabbage, beetroot and salads. Standard on Wednesdays and Fridays.

places.name: Dashen Traditional Restaurant
places.note: Generous fasting platters at lunchtime, when the local crowd fills the room.

places.name: Kategna Restaurant
places.note: Neat, well-balanced beyaynetu; convenient for visitors staying in Bole.

places.name: 2000 Habesha
places.note: Serves beyaynetu alongside meat platters, useful for mixed groups.

food.name: Tere sega and kurt (raw beef)
food.desc: Warm-from-the-butcher raw beef sliced at the table and dipped in mitmita and awaze. A serious Addis ritual, best at a butchery-restaurant.

places.name: Yohannes Kitfo
places.note: Trusted address for raw-meat dishes with its own butchery standards.

places.name: Addis Ababa Restaurant
places.note: Traditional restaurant serving tere sega with injera and spiced dips.

places.name: Dashen Traditional Restaurant
places.note: Local butchery-style plates; ask for kurt with awaze on the side.

food.name: Buna (Ethiopian coffee ceremony)
food.desc: Green beans roasted, ground and brewed in a jebena clay pot, poured in three rounds over incense and popcorn. Coffee was born here.

places.name: Tomoca Coffee
places.note: Roasting and serving since 1953; the city's most famous espresso counter.

places.name: Yod Abyssinia
places.note: Full jebena ceremony performed at your table after dinner.

places.name: Kaldi's Coffee
places.note: Ethiopian chain, handy and consistent for macchiato with local beans.

food.name: Tej and tella
food.desc: Tej is honey wine fermented with gesho hops and drunk from a round berele flask; tella is the cloudy home-brewed barley beer.

places.name: Topia Tej House
places.note: Well-known tej house where you can compare dry and sweet honey wines.

places.name: Yod Abyssinia
places.note: Serves tej in berele flasks with the cultural show; easy introduction.

places.name: 2000 Habesha
places.note: Tej and tella on the menu alongside traditional platters and live music.

landmarks: Holy Trinity Cathedral
Ethiopia's grandest church, resting place of Emperor Haile Selassie, with stunning stained glass and stone architecture blending European and Ethiopian styles.
Meskel Square
The city's dramatic terraced central plaza, famous for the colorful annual Meskel bonfire festival and sweeping views of downtown Addis.
Entoto Mountain
The forested peak overlooking Addis Ababa, home to historic churches and Emperor Menelik II's original palace, offering panoramic city views.
National Museum of Ethiopia
Home to 'Lucy,' the 3.2-million-year-old Australopithecus fossil that rewrote human origins, making this a must for any visitor.
Unity Park
A beautifully restored palace-turned-museum and zoo complex showcasing Ethiopia's imperial history and diverse wildlife within manicured gardens.
Africa Hall
The iconic modernist headquarters of the African Union, adorned with a monumental stained-glass mural symbolizing African unity and liberation.
St. George's Cathedral
An octagonal 1896 church commemorating victory at the Battle of Adwa, notable for its intricate murals and historic Ethiopian art museum.
Red Terror Martyrs' Memorial Museum
A powerful and moving memorial documenting the Derg regime's brutal 1977-78 crackdown, essential for understanding modern Ethiopian history.
Mercato
One of Africa's largest open-air markets, a vibrant, chaotic sprawl of stalls selling everything from spices to textiles, alive with color and energy.
Menelik II Equestrian Statue
A striking bronze monument to the emperor who founded modern Addis Ababa, standing prominently near Piazza and St. George's Cathedral.

intl.time: ~12h, split over 2 days with an overnight stop in Dire Dawa

train.note: The only intercity passenger train is the standard-gauge line to Djibouti, departing from Furi-Lebu (Lebu) station in the south-west of the city; it runs about every second day and through passengers overnight in Dire Dawa. Book online at bookingedr.et (local mobile payment only) or at the station, and bring your passport. The Addis Ababa Light Rail is city tram transit only, not intercity.

intl.to: Moyale border for Kenya, and eastward for Djibouti and Somaliland
intl.op: regional and shared cross-border services — tickets at the terminal, no online booking

bus.note: No online-bookable international coach runs from Addis; cross-border travel to Kenya goes overland via the Moyale border and to Somaliland/Djibouti via the east, mostly on regional or shared services. The main long-distance domestic coach operators are Selam Bus and Sky Bus, running from the Meskel Square / Lamberet area to cities across Ethiopia.

ferry.note: Ethiopia is landlocked, so there are no ferries; the nearest sea access is the port of Djibouti, reachable on the EDR train.
